title: Polynomial-time stable matching in unimodular hypergraphs
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Does there exist a deterministic algorithm that, given any finite hypergraph \(H=(V,E)\) whose vertex–hyperedge incidence matrix is totally unimodular and a strict preference ordering at each vertex over its incident hyperedges, finds a stable matching in time polynomial in the explicit input length? A matching is a collection of pairwise disjoint hyperedges. Stability means that every unchosen hyperedge e contains some vertex v already matched to an edge it strictly prefers to e.
context:
A hyperedge represents a group that could cooperate. Selected groups cannot share members. Stability forbids an unselected group whose members would all prefer forming it to their current situation. The input includes each participant’s ranking, so merely finding disjoint groups is insufficient.

The source explains why total unimodularity together with a classical stable-fractional existence theorem guarantees an integral stable matching. It does not give a general polynomial running-time bound. Hardness of maximizing weight among stable matchings is a different question from finding any stable one.

An August 2026 preprint gives a polynomial-time algorithm for network hypergraphs. In that class the ground elements are arcs of an oriented tree and each hyperedge is a directed tree path. Network hypergraphs are a subclass of unimodular hypergraphs, so this narrows the open frontier without resolving the general target.
why: Tests whether a strong integrality promise can turn guaranteed coalition stability into an efficient algorithm. It extends the computational perspective of classical stable matching while keeping the target independent of optimization over stable outcomes.
status_note: General unimodular stable matching is open in the ICALP 2025 source. Checked against the August 2026 network-hypergraph preprint and subsequent searches on 12 September 2026; no general resolution located. The new special-case theorem is recorded as a preprint result, without an independent proof audit.

progress.text: The source treats structured subclasses and leaves arbitrary unimodular hypergraphs open.

references.title: Stable Hypergraph Matching in Unimodular Hypergraphs
references.authors: Biró, Péter; Csáji, Gergely; Schlotter, Ildikó
references.locator: Unresolved-question passage on page 19; PDF page 19

definitions: Hyperedges are explicitly listed nonempty subsets of V. The incidence matrix A has \(A_{v,e}=1\) if \(v\in e\) and 0 otherwise; it is totally unimodular when every square submatrix has determinant in \(\{- 1,0,1\}\). Each vertex supplies a strict total order on its incident edges and prefers any such edge to remaining unmatched. With M a matching, an edge \(e\notin M\) blocks M exactly when every \(v\in e\) is unmatched or prefers e to its unique incident edge in M. The promise is total unimodularity, with no bound on hyperedge size; all vertex capacities are one. Input length includes every incidence and preference-list entry. The output is any stable M, without a cardinality or weight objective.
answer_criterion: Give a polynomial-time algorithm and prove that its output is stable for every promised instance, or prove that no such deterministic algorithm exists. An NP/PPAD hardness result must retain its complexity assumption. Existence alone, fractional matchings, maximum-weight optimization, or an algorithm for a proper subclass does not settle this search question.
